newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-The Weekend in Australian Sport.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-The Weekend in Australian Sport.

text.p: RUGBY LEAGUE

SYDNEY - The fallout from Friday's Federal Court ruling in favour of media baron Rupert Murdoch's Super League dominated weekend sport, with speculation centring on whether Australian Rugby League (ARL) clubs would jump ship to Super League.
ARL chairman Ken Arthurson brushed aside reports that up to three clubs were already considering whether to leave the ARL.

"I think that's the sort of tactics that they've used from the outset, those scare tactics, to try and make clubs nervous, to try and get them to defect and turn on each other," Arthurson told a news conference.
"But the clubs have remained very strong and very solid and they are determined that they will hang in there with each other."

Arthurson added that the ARL would seek extra financial backing from pay-TV operator Optus as they attempt to appeal to the High Court to have Friday's Federal Court appeal ruling in favour of Super League overturned.
The ARL was reported on Sunday to have told their 12 remaining loyal clubs to commit themselves to the game's traditional rulers again next year, while the rumour mill worked overtime.
Other unsubstantiated media reports said this year's grand finalists St George, Parramatta and even Sydney City were among clubs considering a move to Super League.
One television report, which gave no names and quoted no sources, even suggested St George was considering a move to Melbourne.

South Sydney chief executive Darrell Bampton told reporters his club and the Gold Coast had already told the ARL they would play again next year, while Parramatta and St George officials urged the ARL to enter peace talks with Super League.
Applications for clubs to play in next year's ARL competition must be lodged by October 11.
SYDNEY - The Super League juggernaut was working overtime at the weekend, announcing wide-ranging plans for the future as well as rule changes for their 1997 competition in Australia.

It appears rugby league in Australia will be played under two sets of rules next year, with Super League's International Board announcing on Sunday a number of rule changes that will bring Australia into line with Britain and France.
The most radical of the changes announced on Sunday involves the restart after a try, with the scoring side now kicking off instead of the team who conceded the try.
All scrums will be set 20 metres in-field from touch instead of 10 and there will be no striking for the ball by defending players in play-the-balls.
There will also be an extra tackle added to the existing tackle count of six for players who pick up the ball from kicks by the opposing side instead of allowing it to roll into touch.
The unlimited replacement rule was targeted by Super League as their next most likely change, while the introduction of a "video referee" for controversial decisions was also mooted.

Other proposals suggested in a busy weekend for all concerned included playing part of next year's Super League-aligned World Cup in Australia, while Super League International Board chairman Maurice Lindsay said there would be no test series this year between Britain and Australia.
Australian Rules club Carlton was even reported on Saturday to be interested in having a Super League side play at its Optus Oval home ground next year.

Carlton general manager Stephen Gough told reporters the club had registered the name Carlton Rugby League Club this year at the same time it lodged the name of its team in the national soccer league.
"We've always been a supporter of league," Gough said.
"We've held games before at Optus Oval and we are always looking at utilising the ground."
PORT MORESBY - In the midst of the Super League furore, Bob Fulton's ARL-backed Kangaroos took on the remnants of Papua New Guinea's ARL-loyal forces in a test on Sunday.
The PNG Palais got off to a great start when halfback Adrian Lam scored a clever individual try to give his side an unlikely 6-0 lead after 16 minutes.
The Kangaroos soon got over the shock and ground out a 52-6 win, with utility player Andrew Johns snaring a personal tally of 20 points from a try and eight goals.
Rod Wishart, Wayne Bartrim, Michael Buettner and Tim Brasher all scored two tries each for the Australians in front of 8,000 boisterous PNG fans.

But despite the size of the win the Super League debate was never far away, with coach Bob Fulton telling reporters he was happy with the side's win despite a limited time to prepare and the disruption of Friday's Federal Court ruling.
"These sorts of things happen in these types of games where you are expected to win convincingly," Fulton said.
"But we got our mind on the job. After they scored their try when Lam went over, you know we scored 28 points in the first half, which is pretty good.
"But we dropped the ball and we had to do a fair bit of it in the first half ... you couldn't ask much more given the limited preparation and what's gone on in the last few days.
"It's on people's minds. You can't relate it to points on the board, but it does relate to your preparation," he said.
- - - - CRICKET

PATIALA, India - Middle-order batsman Michael Bevan opened his side's tour of India with a blazing unbeaten century as Australia reached 358 for eight declared in their first innings against the Indian Board President's XI on Sunday.
The Indian President's selection got off to a shaky start in reply, with pace bowler Paul Reiffel striking twice to have them 85 for two at the the close of the second day.
Reiffel removed both openers, including test player Sanjay Manjrekar, to have the Indians 2-13 from seven overs.
Bevan's 29th first class century came from 157 balls before captain Mark Taylor declared the innings closed. The dashing lefthander has not played in a test since England's 1994-95 tour of Australia.
Earlier, opener Michael Slater was out for 56 after adding four runs to his overnight score when Australia had reached 122 for one on a rain-shortened first day's play on Saturday.
Slater, who was dropped when on 29, posted his half-century in 86 deliveries and struck medium pacer David Johnson for a six over fine-leg and hit three boundaries.
Taylor, who opted to bat first after winning the toss, edged an outswinger from Doddanarasiah Ganesh to wicketkeeper Saba Karim after scoring 20. Ricky Ponting made 58.
The match, Australia's first of a month-long tour, was delayed after a storm on Thursday blew away the covers, exposing the pitch to torrential rain.
The three-day match is Australia's only tour fixture before Thursday's start to a one-off test against India in New Delhi.
MOTOR RACING
BATHURST - Craig Lowndes became the youngest driver to win the Bathurst 1000 at Mount Panorama when he scored a decisive victory in Sunday's wet and incident-packed race.

Lowndes, 22, shared the honours with his 24-year-old Holden Commodore co-driver Greg Murphy. He also became only the second driver after Peter Brock in 1978 and 1980 to win the Australian touring car championship, the Sandown 500 and the Bathurst title in the same year.
"This is fantastic," Lowndes told reporters. "Greg and I have had a great run. This wraps up the year brilliantly."
Dick Johnson and John Bowe drove their Falcon into second while Tony Longhurst and Steve Ellery were third in another Falcon.
Commodore drivers Wayne Gardner and Neil Crompton were fourth but later complained that a long hold-up behind a pace car had cost them a place.
Brock was fifth and defending champion Larry Perkins sixth.
The early stages of the race were driven in a torrential downpour, which triggered several accidents and brought pace cars out on to the track as officials cleared the wreckage.

Pole qualifier Glenn Seton lost any hope of victory with engine problems in his Falcon but he was luckier than former Formula One world champion Alan Jones, who passed Lowndes in the early stages before his Falcon spectacularly burst into flames when a fuel line ruptured.
GOLF
MELBOURNE - Former Australian Open champion Robert Allenby returned home in Melbourne on Sunday after being injured in a car crash on Spain's Costa del Sol last month.
Allenby, who fractured his sternum in the accident and arrived home in a wheelchair, told waiting reporters he would not play golf again this year.
"I'll probably have maybe two months off completely, just doing nothing, just laying up and resting," Allenby said.

Allenby, who is currently third on the European PGA Tour's money winners' list, said he had gone to Spain to recuperate from an ankle injury and had little memory of the accident at a roundabout on the Spanish resort coast.

"I remember just waking up in hospital in a neck brace, and they're telling me that I've got a fractured sternum, (that) I could have brain damage and I could have a broken neck," he said. Fears of the latter two injuries were unfounded.
In Singapore, Australia's Andrew Bonhomme squandered on Sunday a two-stroke overnight lead to finish fourth in the Singapore PGA Championship at Juron Country Club.

Taiwan's Yeh Chang-ting came from three strokes behind and overtook Bonhomme on the final day with a three-under-par 69 to win the tournament with a 13-under total of 275. Second one stroke behind Yeh was U.S. golfer Fran Quinn.
South Africa's Nico Van Rensburg was third on 11-under. Bonhomme started at 13-under but carded a three-over 75 for equal fourth with Taiwan's Chang Tse-peng and Lin Chih-chen.
RUGBY UNION
ROME - Rugby union could be back on the Olympic programme for the 2004 Games, chairman of the International Rugby Football Board (IRFB) Vernon Pugh said on Saturday.
"We thought it might have been possible for the Sydney Olympics but that has passed us by, but I would expect in 2004 -- if we wish it -- to see rugby in the Olympics," said Pugh.
Pugh said it would not be a 15-a-side tournament -- rather a seven or 10-a-side competition.
Rugby union was last on the programme at the 1924 Games in Paris.
